Page | Congressman Mike Lawler Antisemitism has no place in America, and I am proud to be one of the loudest voices in Congress to call it out and stand up against it. As the representative of one of the largest Jewish communities in the country, I’ve made fighting hatred one of my top priorities in Congress. We’ve witnessed a disturbing surge in antisemitic incidents on college campuses, in our streets, online, and even at houses of worship. It is unacceptable, and I’ve taken concrete action against it.</p> <p style="text-align: center;"> <br /> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Here’s What I’ve Done</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">Introduced the bipartisan <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?documentid=3694"><em>Antisemitism Awareness Act</em></a>, which requires the Department of Education to use the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism when enforcing federal anti-discrimination laws under Title VI, giving administrators and the federal government the tools they need to identify and stop antisemitism on college campuses. In the 118th Congress, the bill passed the House with overwhelming bipartisan support (320-91), and I reintroduced it early in this Congress. I am currently working to push it across the finish line.</p> <p dir="ltr">I have also partnered with my Democratic colleague, Rep. Dan Goldman from New York City, on the <a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/9211"><em>Jewish American Security Act</em></a>. This legislation significantly increases funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program, helping synagogues, Jewish schools, and other religious institutions strengthen their physical security. The bill also establishes an Antisemitism Coordinator at the Department of Education an

Page | Congressman Mike Lawler <strong><span style="font-size: 18px;">Congressman Lawler Stands With Every Hudson Valley Student</span></strong></p> <p dir="ltr">My focus with education policy has always been simple: supporting strong local schools, making higher education more affordable, and preparing the next generation for success. Every child in every zip code deserves the same opportunity to thrive, and I have consistently used my position to advance quality education initiatives.</p> <p dir="ltr">Whether it’s lowering the cost of student loans, expanding access to professional development opportunities, supporting access to career and technical education, or keeping dangerous drugs out of our schools, I’ve prioritized delivering real results for Hudson Valley families and students. </p> <p dir="ltr">Below is the work I’m doing to strengthen education from early childhood through higher education.</p> <p style="text-align: center;"> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Supporting Our Local Schools</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">As a proud graduate of the Hudson Valley public school system and a parent myself, I know how critical strong local schools are to our communities.</p> <p dir="ltr">I've fought back against proposals that would cut Foundation Aid to nearly half the schools in our district while spending billions on other priorities.</p> <p dir="ltr">During my time in the State Assembly and now in Congress, I’ve consistently pushed for fairer funding formulas so that schools in Rockland, Putnam, Westchester, and Dutchess Counties receive the resources they need and deserve.</p> <p dir="ltr">I’ve also stood up for age-appropriate curriculum and the right of parents to be involved in their children’s education while teaching t

Page | Congressman Mike Lawler My approach is straightforward: lower utility costs for working and middle-class families, strengthen grid reliability, promote American energy independence, and protect the clean air, clean water, and natural beauty that make the Hudson Valley such a great place to live.</p> <p dir="ltr">Whether it’s advocating for an all-of-the-above energy strategy, pushing to rebuild Indian Point, streamlining permitting for critical infrastructure projects, or advancing bipartisan efforts to address extreme heat and protect our watershed and the Appalachian Trail, I’ve focused my efforts on delivering practical solutions that directly benefit our communities.</p> <p dir="ltr">Below is some of the work I’m doing to make energy more affordable and reliable while protecting our environment.<br /> </p> <p style="text-align: center;"><strong> <br /> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </strong></p> <strong> An All-of-the-Above Energy Strategy</strong> <p dir="ltr">Since my first day in Congress, I’ve supported an all-of-the-above energy strategy that strengthens our electric grid, promotes American energy independence, lowers costs, and protects our environment.</p> <p dir="ltr">That means investing in nuclear, natural gas, hydropower, renewables, and other reliable energy sources. A strong energy future requires dependable baseload power alongside renewable energy, so families aren’t left paying higher bills or dealing with an unreliable grid.</p> <p dir="ltr">Natural gas remains an important part of New York’s energy mix and has helped reduce carbon emissions by replacing coal. Blocking pipelines and banning responsible domestic production only drives up prices and forces us to depend on energy produced elsewhere, often under weaker environmental standards.</p> <p dir="ltr">I’ve also c

Page | Congressman Mike Lawler As Vice Chair of Communications for the House Financial Services Committee, I’m focused on ensuring our financial system works for Hudson Valley families, small businesses, community banks, and the next generation of American innovators, not just the biggest institutions on Wall Street.</p> <p style="text-align: center;"> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </p> <p dir="ltr">This Congress, the Committee has delivered meaningful, bipartisan progress on community banking, capital formation, consumer protection, and the future of digital finance. My priority has been clear: expand opportunity, reduce unnecessary regulatory burdens, protect people from scams, and keep the United States the global leader in financial services.</p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Supporting Main Street</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">Local banks and credit unions are the backbone of our economy. They know their communities, they lend to small businesses, and they help families buy homes and build wealth. Yet for too long, one-size-fits-all regulations have treated them the same as the largest global banks.</p> <p dir="ltr">That’s why I strongly supported the <a href="https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/6955"><em>Main Street Capital Access Act</em></a><em>,</em> which passed the House with robust bipartisan support. This legislation revitalizes community bank formation, right-sizes capital and regulatory requirements, and allows local lenders to focus on serving customers instead of navigating unnecessary compliance burdens.</p> <p dir="ltr">Strong community banks mean more capital flowing into the Hudson Valley and communities across America.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Expanding Access to Capital for Entrepreneurs</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">Ameri

Page | Congressman Mike Lawler As Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa, I’ve made strengthening America’s role on the world stage one of my highest priorities in Congress.</p> <p dir="ltr">From supporting our allies and regional partners abroad to expanding the Abraham Accords, cutting off Iran’s funding for terrorism, and reforming the State Department to ensure our diplomats are equipped for 21st-century challenges, I’ve focused on delivering results that protect American interests and promote stability.</p> <p dir="ltr">Below is an overview of the work I’m doing as Subcommittee Chairman and as a member of the full House Foreign Affairs Committee.</p> <p style="text-align: center;"> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Leading On the Middle East &amp; North Africa</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">In January 2025, I was <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=3594">honored to be named Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee</a> on the Middle East and North Africa. Page | Congressman Mike Lawler Immigrant communities make the Hudson Valley and so much of our country what they are today. We need a functional legal immigration system that prioritizes merit-based immigration, keeps families united, and ensures good people can achieve the American Dream through doable steps instead of an outdated, cumbersome process. As the husband of a naturalized citizen, I’ve seen firsthand how difficult and inefficient the current system can be for those who play by the rules. I know that we can do better.</p> <p dir="ltr">At the same time, to combat illegal immigration, we need strong borders. Under the previous administration, more than 10 million migrants entered the country illegally. Catch-and-release policies, a broken asylum system, and sanctuary policies in places like New York create chaos, endanger public safety, and place enormous burdens on local police precincts. Not only that, but open border policies have allowed fentanyl to make its way into our communities.</p> <p style="text-align: center;"> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Reforming Our Badly Broken Immigration System</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">As President Reagan said, America is a shining city on a hill for those seeking a better life. I believe that we must do everything we can to keep that vision alive.</p> <p dir="ltr">Unfortunately, the current process for legally immigrating to the United States is broken and has not been meaningfully reformed in nearly 40 years. We face real workforce shortages in critical fields like healthcare, agriculture, construction, and engineering, yet the legal immigration process remains slow, complicated, and disconnected from America’s economic needs.</p> <p dir="ltr">I support reforms that modernize the legal immigration system, reduce unnecessary delays, and prioritize th

Page | Congressman Mike Lawler Bringing federal resources home and delivering real results for the communities I represent are among my top priorities in Congress. From public safety and infrastructure to honoring local heroes and helping individual constituents, my focus is always on strengthening the Hudson Valley.</p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Honoring Local Heroes</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">The Hudson Valley has produced extraordinary individuals whose courage, service, and contributions deserve lasting national recognition.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">I introduced the bipartisan <em><a href="https://lawler.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=4789">Welles Remy Crowther Congressional Gold Medal Act</a>&nbsp;</em>to posthumously award one of our nation’s highest civilian honors to the “Man in the Red Bandana.” Welles, a volunteer firefighter from Upper Nyack and a proud son of Rockland County, selflessly returned again and again to the South Tower on September 11, 2001, to guide people to safety.&nbsp;</p> <p dir="ltr">His bravery saved numerous lives before he made the ultimate sacrifice. His story continues to inspire our community and the country, and this legislation will ensure Congress permanently recognizes his legacy.</p> <p dir="ltr">I also reintroduced legislation to award a <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=3869">Congressional Gold Medal to the late James Earl Jones</a>, a longtime resident of the Hudson Valley. Page | Congressman Mike Lawler <span style="font-size: 16px;">Women’s healthcare has historically been underfunded and lacking prioritization by the federal government and the healthcare industry. This is unacceptable. It’s why I have spent my time in Congress working to strengthen accessible and affordable care for women. That includes safeguarding access to contraception and to medications like mifepristone, as well as promoting enhanced screening options for cancers that predominantly affect women.</span></p> <p dir="ltr"><span style="font-size: 16px;">On the issue of abortion, I have consistently and strongly opposed any effort to establish a national ban. Page | Congressman Mike Lawler Protecting Social Security, expanding affordable housing, and ensuring older Americans are treated with dignity are among my top priorities in Congress. I am committed to standing up for seniors across the Hudson Valley and making sure they have access to the services and support they have earned.</p> <p style="text-align: center;"> <a href="https://lawler.house.gov/forms/form/?ID=8" style="background-color:#003366;color:white;padding:14px 24px;text-decoration:none;border-radius:6px;font-weight:bold;display:inline-block;"> SIGN UP FOR MY E-NEWSLETTER FOR UPDATES</a> <br /> </p> <p dir="ltr"><strong>Protecting Seniors’ Access to Care &amp; Social Security Benefits</strong></p> <p dir="ltr">When the Social Security Administration announced plans to close its Office of Hearing Operations in White Plains, I fought to ensure Hudson Valley seniors would continue to have access to the services they rely on.
